title: Revenue architecture rebuild · vertical SaaS
description: Redesigned the full GTM operating model for a vertical SaaS at Series A: ICP definition with real scoring criteria, pipeline logic rebuilt around buyer behaviour, CRM architecture, content engine, and a unified analytics layer. Delivered as one integrated system.
problem: The company had product-market fit and early revenue, but no coherent GTM system. Deals came from founder relationships. ICP was loosely defined. Pipeline stages were labels, not behavioural signals. There was no single view of what drove revenue versus what was noise.
system: Three-phase rebuild. Phase one: ICP sharpening with the founding team — from 'mid-market B2B SaaS' to specific firmographic and behavioural criteria that could score any prospect consistently. Phase two: CRM overhaul — stage redefinition around buyer signals, contact normalisation, and pipeline logic that reflected reality. Phase three: content engine and analytics layer tied to pipeline so every investment was traceable to revenue outcomes.
artifact: CRM architecture and stage playbooks. ICP scoring framework with decision criteria. Content engine with editorial calendar aligned to buying stages. GA4 and Amplitude analytics layer tied to pipeline events. Operator handoff manual so the system ran without ongoing oversight.
outcome: ICP-to-SQL conversion lifted 35%. Founder dependency on active pipeline dropped from near-100% to under 40% in 90 days as the team could operate the system independently. Revenue attribution became visible for the first time: which channels, which segments, which content produced qualified pipeline.
